inputs.label: Etsy app API key (keystring)
inputs.name: ETSY_KEYSTRING
setupSteps: In the Etsy Developers portal, open your app and copy its keystring (API key).
This value is sent as the `x-api-key` header and used as the OAuth client id (PKCE public client).
Set the app's OAuth callback / redirect URI to the redirect URI below.

inputs.label: Etsy shared secret (optional)
inputs.name: ETSY_SHARED_SECRET
setupSteps: Optional: copy the shared secret from the same Etsy app.
Not required by the v3 PKCE public-client flow; stored for completeness / future use.

inputs.label: OAuth client ID

setupSteps: In GitHub Developer settings, create a new OAuth App (an OAuth App, not a GitHub App — GitHub Apps ignore OAuth scopes).
Set the Homepage URL to your instance URL, and the Authorization callback URL to the redirect URI below.
Register the application, then generate a new client secret.
Copy the Client ID and client secret here.

inputs.help: The link opens gitlab.com. For a self-managed GitLab, create the application on your own instance instead (the same User settings → Applications page there); the worker's GITLAB_URL must then name that instance.
inputs.label: OAuth application ID
inputs.name: CLIENT_ID
setupSteps: In GitLab, open User settings → Applications (or a group's Settings → Applications) and add a new application.
Set the Redirect URI to the value below and leave Confidential checked.
Select the scopes: api, write_repository, and read_user.
Save the application, then copy the Application ID and Secret here.

inputs.label: OAuth client ID
inputs.name: CLIENT_ID
setupSteps: In the Google Cloud Console, create a project (or pick an existing one).

Enable the APIs gadgets should reach: Gmail, Google Docs, Google Drive, Google Sheets, Google Slides, Google Calendar, Google Chat, People (for Chat names and directory search), and BigQuery (APIs & Services > Library).

For Chat, open the Google Chat API's Configuration tab, set an app name, avatar URL and description, turn off interactive features, and save. Without it Chat reads work but every send, edit and reaction fails.
Configure the OAuth consent screen (External) and add yourself as a test user while the app is unverified.
Create an OAuth client ID of type "Web application" and add the redirect URI below.
Copy the client ID and client secret here.

inputs.help: Agents reach SharePoint, OneDrive, Outlook and Outlook Calendar as the user who connected, through this app registration's delegated permissions, so they can never open more than that user can.
inputs.label: Application (client) ID
inputs.name: CLIENT_ID
setupSteps: In the Microsoft Entra admin center, open App registrations and select New registration.

Choose Accounts in this organizational directory only (the package README describes a multitenant setup, which needs settings this wizard doesn't collect), add a Web redirect URI with the value below, and register.

Under API permissions, add Microsoft Graph delegated permissions: openid, profile, email, offline_access and User.Read; for SharePoint, Sites.ReadWrite.All and Files.ReadWrite.All; for Outlook, Mail.ReadWrite, Mail.ReadWrite.Shared, Mail.Send, Mail.Send.Shared, MailboxSettings.ReadWrite, People.Read and User.ReadBasic.All; for Calendar, Calendars.ReadWrite, Calendars.ReadWrite.Shared, MailboxSettings.Read, People.Read and User.ReadBasic.All. A wizard install asks users for this full set, so granting less makes connecting fail; a deployment that wants read-only access or only selected sites sets the environment variables the package README describes.
Select Grant admin consent, so users aren't asked to approve each permission themselves.
Under Certificates & secrets, create a client secret, and note when it expires: connections stop refreshing once it does.
Copy the Application (client) ID and Directory (tenant) ID from the Overview page, and the secret's Value (not its ID), here.

inputs.help: A Scoped OAuth app registered on your own PagerDuty account. Only users of that account can connect, and each sees only what PagerDuty shows them.
inputs.label: OAuth Client ID
inputs.name: CLIENT_ID
setupSteps: Sign in to your PagerDuty account as a Manager, Global Admin or Account Owner, open Integrations > Developer Tools > App Registration, and select New App.
Give it a name and a description. Under Functionality, tick "OAuth 2.0" only, and continue.
Set Authorization to "Scoped OAuth". The form starts on "Classic User OAuth", which the gatekeeper can't use.
Add the Redirect URL below.
Under Permission Scope, grant these permissions: Incidents (read and write), Schedules (read and write), and read access to Services, Teams, Users, On-Calls, Priorities and Escalation Policies.
Select Register App, and copy the Client ID and Client Secret here.

inputs.label: OAuth client ID
inputs.name: CLIENT_ID
setupSteps: Create a Slack app (from scratch) in the workspace you want gadgets to read.
Under OAuth & Permissions, add the redirect URL below.
Enable token rotation (OAuth & Permissions > Token Rotation) — tokens are then short-lived and refreshed automatically.
Copy the app's Client ID and Client Secret (Basic Information > App Credentials) here.

inputs.help: X bills every API request to this app's prepaid credits, so the app's owner pays for every user's reads and posts. Posts containing a link cost more than other posts.
inputs.label: OAuth 2.0 Client ID
inputs.name: CLIENT_ID
setupSteps: In the X Developer Console, create a Project and an App.
Under User authentication settings, enable OAuth 2.0 with the type "Web App, Automated App or Bot" and the permission "Read and write".
Set the Callback URI to the value below, and give the app a website URL.
Buy credits and set a spending limit: X bills every request this app makes.
X requires its prior approval before an app posts AI-generated replies; replies drafted by agents are sent only once a user approves each one, but the obligation is the app owner's.
Copy the OAuth 2.0 Client ID and Client Secret here.
